add-216.title: Sudanese Helo-Mur (Abreh) Drink
add-216.prepTime: a week to sprout the sorghum
add-216.culturalNotes: Helo-mur is Sudan's most famous Ramadan drink, and making its flakes is a communal ritual weeks before the month. Ready-made flakes are sold in Sudanese shops, cutting the work to soaking.

add-216-i3.name: Helo-mur spices: cinnamon, cardamom, ginger, cloves, black cumin, fenugreek

add-216-i6.name: To serve: sugar and cold water

instructions.1: Zariaa: soak the sorghum a day, spread on a damp cloth and cover until it sprouts (5-7 days), then sun-dry and grind.
instructions.2: Mix the sprouted flour with the sorghum flour, ground spices and soaked dates, add water into a batter and leave two days to ferment.
instructions.3: Spread the mixture very thin on a hot griddle until dry, browned and crisp flakes form, then break and store them.
instructions.4: To serve: soak the flakes in cold water for 2-3 hours until their flavour and colour dissolve.
instructions.5: Strain, sweeten with sugar and serve ice-cold at iftar.

add-217.title: Dates with Milk (Balah bel Laban)
add-217.culturalNotes: Dates with milk is the Ramadan iftar drink in Egypt, giving quick energy after fasting. Soaking the dates first gives a velvety texture with no bits.

add-217-i4.name: Crushed nuts and coconut to garnish

instructions.1: Wash and pit the dates and soak in a cup of the milk for an hour until soft.
instructions.2: Blend the dates with the soaking milk until completely smooth, then add the rest of the milk and blend a minute.
instructions.3: Serve cold or warm with a sprinkle of nuts, or leave the dates in pieces in the milk without blending, as you prefer.

add-218.title: Creamy Cheddar Cheese Sauce
add-218.culturalNotes: Grating the cheddar yourself rather than using pre-grated makes it melt smoothly, since pre-grated contains anti-caking starch. Don't let the sauce boil after adding the cheese or it turns grainy.

instructions.1: Melt the butter, add the flour and stir a minute without colouring.
instructions.2: Whisk in the milk gradually so it doesn't lump, and cook until slightly thickened.
instructions.3: Lower the heat right down and add the cheddar in batches, stirring until completely melted, then the mustard and paprika.
instructions.4: Serve warm with nachos, fries and burgers, thinning with a little milk if it thickens.

add-219.title: Baked Potato Kibbeh Tray
add-219.culturalNotes: Potato kibbeh is an easier and cheaper version of traditional kibbeh, and the bulgur gives it the firmness and familiar kibbeh texture.

instructions.1: Knead the potato with the bulgur, egg and spices, adding flour if soft, until the dough holds together.
instructions.2: Soften the onion, then cook the meat with the spices, and add the pine nuts.
instructions.3: Spread half the potato dough in a greased tray, spread the filling, then cover with the rest of the dough and smooth with a wet hand.
instructions.4: Score the top in a crisscross with a knife and brush with ghee.
instructions.5: Bake at 200°C for 35-40 minutes until the top is golden and crisp.
instructions.6: Serve with yogurt and green salad.

add-220.title: Lebanese Bayaz (Onion, Parsley and Sumac Salad)
add-220.culturalNotes: Rubbing the onion with salt and sumac takes away its sharpness and makes it soft and tangy; it is the classic partner of grills in Lebanese restaurants.

instructions.1: Rub the sliced onion with the salt and sumac between your fingers for a minute until it softens and turns purple.
instructions.2: Add the parsley and toss.
instructions.3: Drizzle with olive oil and lemon if you like and serve at once with grills, kofta and shawarma.

add-221.title: Seasoned Baked Potato Wedges
add-221.culturalNotes: Soaking to remove starch, then drying well, is the secret of crisp oven wedges without frying.

instructions.1: Scrub the potatoes well, halve each lengthwise, then cut each half into 3-4 thick wedges.
instructions.2: Soak in cold water for 15 minutes to remove the starch, then dry completely.
instructions.3: Toss with the oil, spices and salt until coated.
instructions.4: Spread skin-side down on a lined tray and bake at 220°C for 30-35 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and crisp.
instructions.5: Sprinkle with Parmesan while hot and serve with garlic sauce or ketchup.

add-222.title: Cheesy Garlic Bread
add-222.culturalNotes: Wrapping the bread in foil first lets the garlic butter soak in, and opening it at the end gives the crunch.

add-222-i6.name: A pinch of salt and oregano

instructions.1: Mix the soft butter with the garlic, parsley, salt and oregano.
instructions.2: Slice the bread diagonally without cutting all the way through, or split lengthwise.
instructions.3: Spread the garlic butter inside the slices and top with the cheese.
instructions.4: Wrap in foil and bake at 200°C for 8 minutes, then open the foil and bake 3-4 minutes until the cheese melts and the bread crisps.
instructions.5: Serve hot with pasta or soup.

add-223.title: Slow-Simmered Bone Broth
add-223.culturalNotes: Vinegar helps extract minerals and collagen from the bones, and a successful broth turns to jelly when chilled.

add-223-i1.name: Beef, lamb or chicken bones (with marrow and joints)

add-223-i6.name: Garlic, bay leaf, peppercorns and cinnamon stick

add-223-i7.name: Water
add-223-i7.standardAmount: to cover the bones by 5 cm

instructions.1: Roast the bones at 220°C for 30 minutes until browned (optional, for a darker, richer broth).
instructions.2: Put the bones in a large pot, cover with water, add the vinegar and leave 30 minutes before heating.
instructions.3: Bring to the boil and skim the foam, then add the vegetables and spices.
instructions.4: Simmer on the lowest possible heat for 8-12 hours (4 hours for chicken), topping up with water if needed.
instructions.5: Strain, cool, skim the fat and keep in the fridge 5 days or freeze; salt when using.

add-224.title: Iced Mocha
add-224.culturalNotes: Mocha is a mix of coffee and chocolate. Freezing coffee into ice cubes instead of plain ice stops the drink from getting diluted.

instructions.1: Dissolve the coffee and sugar in the warm water and let cool slightly.
instructions.2: Drizzle lines of chocolate sauce inside the glass.
instructions.3: Whisk or blend the coffee with the milk and a spoon of chocolate sauce until frothy.
instructions.4: Fill the glass with ice, pour the mocha over and top with whipped cream and a sprinkle of cocoa.

add-225.title: Homemade Dessert Ashta (Clotted-Style Cream)
add-225.culturalNotes: A stable ashta that doesn't run in the oven or when cut, with little sugar because Middle Eastern sweets are soaked in syrup.

instructions.1: Dissolve the cornflour, cream powder and sugar in the cold milk, then stir constantly over medium heat until very thick.
instructions.2: Remove from the heat, add the orange-blossom water and let it cool to lukewarm, stirring now and then.
instructions.3: Add the canned cream and whisk until smooth and creamy.
instructions.4: Cover with cling film touching the surface and chill; use to fill qatayef, kunafa and basbousa and to decorate desserts.

add-226.title: Indian Chapati
add-226.culturalNotes: Chapati is an everyday bread in India, East Africa and Yemen. Rolling it with ghee then rolling out again gives soft layers.

instructions.1: Mix the flour, salt and oil, add the water gradually and knead into a smooth, soft dough; rest 20 minutes.
instructions.2: Divide into 10 balls, roll each into a thin round, brush with ghee, fold, coil into a spiral and roll out again (for layers).
instructions.3: Heat an iron or non-stick pan and cook each bread until bubbles appear, then flip, brush with ghee and press with a spatula until it puffs and spots golden.
instructions.4: Stack the breads under a cloth and serve with curry and masala.

add-227.title: Karak Chai
add-227.culturalNotes: Karak is the favourite street drink of the Gulf, originally from Indian chai. Letting it boil up several times gives its creamy body and concentrated flavour.

add-227-i2.name: Loose black tea or tea granules

instructions.1: Boil the water with the cardamom, cloves and cinnamon for 3 minutes.
instructions.2: Add the tea and sugar and simmer on low heat for 5-7 minutes until strong and dark.
instructions.3: Add the evaporated milk and saffron and let it rise, then lower the heat and let it rise two or three more times.
instructions.4: Strain and serve hot in small cups.

add-228.title: Egyptian Savory Qaraqeesh (Salted Eid Kaak)
add-228.culturalNotes: Savory qaraqeesh are baked alongside Eid kahk in Egypt and served with tea; fennel and anise give them their distinctive aroma.

instructions.1: Rub the flour with the ghee until fully absorbed.
instructions.2: Add the yeast, sesame, fennel, anise, nigella, sugar and salt, then the warm water gradually, and bring together lightly.
instructions.3: Cover and rest 30-45 minutes until doubled.
instructions.4: Roll part of the dough into a long strip and cut diagonally into fingers, or shape small rings; arrange on trays and rest 10 minutes.
instructions.5: Bake at 180°C until the bases colour, then turn on the grill to lightly brown the tops.
instructions.6: Let cool completely to crisp up and store in airtight tins.

add-229.title: Crispy Orange Cookies
add-229.culturalNotes: Economical Eid cookies; the zest carries more flavour than the juice because the aromatic oils are in the peel.

add-229-i8.name: Vanilla and a pinch of salt

instructions.1: Cream the butter with the icing sugar and zest, then add the eggs and vanilla.
instructions.2: Add the flour, baking powder and salt alternately with the orange juice into a smooth dough.
instructions.3: Shape with a cookie press or piping bag, or roll and cut with cutters, onto lined trays.
instructions.4: Bake at 180°C for 12-15 minutes until the edges colour.
instructions.5: Let cool completely to crisp and store in airtight tins.

add-230.title: Hijazi Almond 'Coffee' (Milk and Almond Drink)
add-230.culturalNotes: Almond 'coffee' is a winter drink from the Hijaz, called coffee although it contains none. It is served to guests on cold winter nights.

instructions.1: Blanch the almonds for 2 minutes, peel and crush coarsely.
instructions.2: Dissolve the rice flour and sugar in the cold milk, then heat over medium heat, stirring constantly.
instructions.3: Add the almonds and cardamom and simmer on low heat 10 minutes, stirring, until slightly thickened.
instructions.4: Add the saffron or rose water and serve hot in cups with almond pieces.

add-231.title: Three-Cheese Mint Samosa
add-231.culturalNotes: Feta gives saltiness, mozzarella the stretch and cheddar a strong flavour, while mint adds freshness to balance the richness.

add-231-i1.name: Feta or salty white cheese, crumbled

add-231-i4.name: Dried mint (or ½ cup fresh, chopped)

add-231-i8.name: Flour and water paste to seal

instructions.1: Mix the three cheeses with the mint, nigella seeds and egg until combined.
instructions.2: Put a spoonful of filling on the edge of each sheet and fold into successive triangles to the end.
instructions.3: Seal the end with the flour paste.
instructions.4: Fry in hot oil until golden on both sides and drain on kitchen paper.
instructions.5: Serve hot with the cheese stretchy.

add-232.title: Chicken, Corn and Mayo Samosa
add-232.culturalNotes: A creative filling children love; samosas can be made and frozen before frying for the Ramadan table.

add-232-i1.name: Boiled chicken breast, finely chopped or shredded

add-232-i6.name: Garlic powder, paprika, salt and black pepper

instructions.1: Mix the chicken with the corn, mayonnaise, cheese, parsley and spices into a creamy filling that holds together.
instructions.2: Fill the sheets and fold into triangles, sealing the end with a flour-and-water paste.
instructions.3: Fry in hot oil until golden, or brush with oil and bake at 200°C for 15 minutes.
instructions.4: Serve hot with sweet chilli sauce.

add-233.title: Classic French Chocolate Mousse
add-233.culturalNotes: Classic French mousse uses raw eggs, so use very fresh or pasteurised eggs. Folding gently keeps it light.

add-233-i2.name: Large eggs, separated, at room temperature

add-233-i6.name: Chocolate shavings or berries to decorate

instructions.1: Melt the chocolate over a water bath and let it cool to lukewarm.
instructions.2: Stir the yolks one at a time into the lukewarm chocolate, then the vanilla.
instructions.3: Whip the cream to soft peaks, and whisk the whites with the icing sugar until firm.
instructions.4: Fold the cream into the chocolate gently, then the whites in two additions with a folding motion so the air isn't lost.
instructions.5: Divide into glasses and chill at least 4 hours; decorate before serving.

add-234.title: Fresh Mango Juice
add-234.culturalNotes: Very ripe mangoes provide most of the sweetness. The best varieties for juice are Owais, Zebdia and Fass.

instructions.1: Peel the mangoes and cut the flesh away from the stone.
instructions.2: Blend with the water, sugar and lemon until completely smooth.
instructions.3: Strain if you prefer a light juice and serve chilled at once.
instructions.4: For mango with milk, use cold milk instead of water and add a scoop of vanilla ice cream.

add-235.title: Watermelon Mint Juice
add-235.culturalNotes: Watermelon needs no water because it is almost all water. Freezing watermelon cubes to use instead of ice keeps the flavour concentrated.

instructions.1: Cut the watermelon into cubes and remove the seeds.
instructions.2: Blend with the lemon, mint and sugar for a few seconds until liquid.
instructions.3: Strain if you like and serve at once over ice.

add-236.title: Classic Vanilla Custard
add-236.culturalNotes: Pouring the hot milk onto the yolks gradually (tempering) stops the eggs curdling. Homemade custard with yolks is far richer than custard powder.

instructions.1: Heat the milk until almost boiling.
instructions.2: Whisk the yolks with the sugar and cornflour until pale and smooth.
instructions.3: Pour a third of the hot milk gradually onto the yolks, whisking, then return the mixture to the pan.
instructions.4: Stir constantly over medium heat until thick and boiling for a minute, then remove and add the vanilla and butter.
instructions.5: Pour into serving dishes, cover with cling film touching the surface so no skin forms, chill and serve with fruit.

add-237.title: Stovetop Popcorn
add-237.culturalNotes: Leaving a gap for steam makes the popcorn crisp rather than chewy, and removing it as soon as the popping slows stops the bottom burning.

add-237-i5.name: Extras: cheese powder, caramel or paprika

instructions.1: Heat the oil in a wide, heavy pot over medium-high heat with 3 test kernels.
instructions.2: When the three pop, add the rest of the kernels, cover leaving a small gap for steam, and shake the pot now and then.
instructions.3: When the popping slows to two seconds between pops, take the pot off the heat at once.
instructions.4: Tip the popcorn into a large bowl and toss with the salt, butter and extras.

add-238.title: Grilled Corn on the Cob
add-238.culturalNotes: Charcoal-grilled corn is the classic summer snack of the Nile Corniche and Alexandria. Rubbing the cob with a lemon slice dipped in salt and chilli is a popular touch.

instructions.1: Remove the husks and silk, and boil the cobs 5 minutes beforehand if you want to shorten the grilling.
instructions.2: Grill over charcoal, a direct gas flame or a hot grill, turning constantly, until the kernels brown with a few black spots, 10-15 minutes.
instructions.3: Brush with butter while hot, sprinkle with salt, squeeze over lemon and add a pinch of chilli.

add-239.title: Chicken and Vegetable Crêpes
add-239.culturalNotes: Resting the batter before cooking makes the crêpes softer and less likely to tear. Crêpes can be made ahead and frozen between sheets of baking paper.

add-239-i11.name: White sauce or mayonnaise and mustard

add-239-i12.name: Paprika, garlic powder and black pepper

instructions.1: Whisk the flour, eggs, milk, salt and oil into a smooth, lump-free batter and rest 15 minutes.
instructions.2: Heat a lightly greased non-stick pan, pour in a ladleful and swirl to cover the base, cooking a minute each side.
instructions.3: Sauté the onion, peppers and mushrooms, add the chicken and spices, then the sauce, and stir.
instructions.4: Put the filling in the middle of each crêpe, sprinkle with cheese and fold into a roll or triangle.
instructions.5: Return to the pan or oven for a few minutes until the cheese melts.
instructions.6: Serve hot with cheese sauce or ketchup.

add-240.title: Molten Chocolate Lava Cake
add-240.culturalNotes: A hot oven and short time are the secret: the crust sets and the centre stays molten. The ramekins can be filled and chilled until baking, adding two minutes.

add-240-i7.name: A pinch of salt and vanilla

add-240-i8.name: Cocoa and butter for the moulds

instructions.1: Butter 4 ramekins and dust with cocoa.
instructions.2: Melt the chocolate with the butter over a water bath until smooth.
instructions.3: Whisk the eggs, yolks and sugar until pale, add the melted chocolate, then fold in the flour, salt and vanilla gently.
instructions.4: Divide among the ramekins and bake in an oven preheated to 220°C for 10-12 minutes until the edges set and the centre still wobbles.
instructions.5: Leave just one minute, then turn out onto a plate and serve at once with ice cream.

add-241.title: Buttered Corn Cups
add-241.culturalNotes: A light street snack loved by children; frozen corn gives excellent results all year.

add-241-i4.name: Extras: grated cheese, mayonnaise, paprika, chilli, lemon

instructions.1: Boil the corn in salted water for 5 minutes or heat in the microwave, then drain.
instructions.2: Toss with the butter and salt over the heat for a minute until coated.
instructions.3: Divide into cups and add the extras you like (Mexican street style: mayonnaise, cheese, paprika and lemon).

add-242.title: Homemade Shanklish Cheese
add-242.culturalNotes: Traditional shanklish is aged for weeks until a beneficial mould forms; this is a quick, milder home version eaten after a few days.

instructions.1: Strain the yogurt in a clean cloth hung over a bowl in the fridge for 24 hours until it becomes very dry labneh.
instructions.2: Mix with the salt, chilli and spices.
instructions.3: Shape into balls the size of a small orange with oiled hands.
instructions.4: Arrange on a tray lined with baking paper in a dry, cool, airy place for 3-4 days until the outside dries.
instructions.5: Roll the balls in dried thyme or chilli and keep in a jar covered with olive oil or in the fridge.

add-243.title: Mint Yogurt Sauce
add-243.culturalNotes: A refreshing Indian-style sauce; the little sugar balances the heat of the chilli and lemon. Without yogurt it becomes a green chutney that keeps longer.

instructions.1: Grind the mint, coriander, garlic, chilli, lemon, sugar and salt in a processor into a paste.
instructions.2: Add the olive oil gradually with the processor running.
instructions.3: Mix the paste with the yogurt and serve cold with grills, samosa and pakora; keeps two days in the fridge.

add-244.title: Fruit and Avocado Salad
add-244.culturalNotes: Avocado adds a creamy texture and healthy fats that make the salad more filling; it goes in last so it isn't mashed.

instructions.1: Cube the avocado and sprinkle at once with lemon juice so it doesn't brown.
instructions.2: Cut the rest of the fruit and toss gently with the avocado in a bowl.
instructions.3: Mix the honey with the orange and lemon juice.
instructions.4: Pour the dressing over the fruit, sprinkle with mint and serve cold at once.

add-245.title: Cream of Mushroom Soup
add-245.culturalNotes: Browning the mushrooms until their water evaporates before adding stock gives the soup a deep flavour instead of a boiled-mushroom taste.

instructions.1: Soften the onion in the butter, then the garlic for a minute.
instructions.2: Add the mushrooms and stir on high heat until they release their water, it evaporates and they brown slightly; set a handful aside to garnish.
instructions.3: Sprinkle in the flour and stir a minute, then add the stock gradually and the thyme and simmer 15 minutes.
instructions.4: Blend the soup smooth with a stick blender, or leave it chunky.
instructions.5: Add the cream, nutmeg, salt and pepper, heat without boiling and serve garnished with the browned mushrooms and parsley.

add-246.title: Egyptian-Style Everyday Pasta with Meat Sauce
add-246.culturalNotes: Everyday pasta is the quick weeknight meal of the Egyptian home. The pasta water binds the sauce to the pasta and makes it glossy.

add-246-i8.name: Mixed spice, black pepper and salt

instructions.1: Boil the pasta in salted water until cooked and drain, keeping a cup of the cooking water.
instructions.2: Soften the onion, then cook the meat, garlic and spices until done.
instructions.3: Add the tomato paste, then the tomato juice, and simmer 15 minutes.
instructions.4: Toss the pasta in the sauce with a little of the cooking water and serve sprinkled with roumi cheese.

add-247.title: Soft Homemade Burger Buns
add-247.culturalNotes: Milk, butter and egg give burger buns their familiar softness, and shaping tight balls makes them rise evenly.

instructions.1: Knead the flour, yeast, sugar and salt with the milk and egg, then add the butter and knead 10 minutes until smooth and glossy.
instructions.2: Cover and leave an hour until doubled.
instructions.3: Divide into 8 equal pieces, shape into tight balls, arrange on a lined tray and press lightly.
instructions.4: Leave 45 minutes until puffed, brush with beaten egg and sprinkle with sesame.
instructions.5: Bake at 190°C for 15 minutes until golden.
instructions.6: Cover with a cloth as soon as they come out so they stay soft.

add-248.title: Berry Yogurt Smoothie
add-248.culturalNotes: Yogurt adds protein and good bacteria, and oats make it a filling breakfast.

instructions.1: Put the milk and yogurt in the blender first, then the berries, honey and oats.
instructions.2: Blend until smooth and thick and serve at once.

add-249.title: Egyptian Fino (Samoli) Bread Rolls
add-249.culturalNotes: Fino is Egypt's favourite sandwich bread. Steam in the oven gives it a thin, glossy, crisp crust.

instructions.1: Mix the flour, salt, sugar and yeast, add the warm water and knead, then add the oil and knead 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
instructions.2: Cover and leave an hour until doubled.
instructions.3: Divide into 8 pieces, roll each into a rectangle, then roll up tightly and shape into a long roll with tapered ends.
instructions.4: Arrange on a tray and leave 45 minutes until puffed, then slash lengthwise with a sharp blade.
instructions.5: Bake at 200°C for 20-25 minutes with a tray of water at the bottom of the oven for steam, until golden.

add-250.title: Banana Peanut Butter Smoothie
add-250.culturalNotes: A protein- and energy-rich smoothie, good after exercise or as a quick breakfast.

instructions.1: Put the milk in the blender first, then the banana, peanut butter, honey and extras.
instructions.2: Blend until smooth and thick and serve at once with a pinch of cinnamon.

add-251.title: Breaded Fried Liver
add-251.culturalNotes: Liver toughens if overcooked or salted too early, so fry it quickly over high heat to keep it tender inside.

instructions.1: Pound the liver slices gently to make them thin and even and remove the membranes.
instructions.2: Marinate with the garlic, lemon, cumin and pepper for 30 minutes, adding the salt just before coating.
instructions.3: Coat each slice in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs.
instructions.4: Fry in hot oil for 1½-2 minutes per side until just golden.
instructions.5: Drain and serve at once with lemon, tahini and fries.

add-252.title: Spiced Sausage (Sujuk) Skillet
add-252.culturalNotes: Oriental sausage (Alexandrian sausage or maqaniq) cooks in its own fat, so little oil is needed. Pomegranate molasses gives a tangy Levantine taste.

instructions.1: Cut the sausage into pieces or rings.
instructions.2: Brown the sausage in the oil until coloured and releasing its fat, then lift out.
instructions.3: Soften the onion, garlic and peppers in the same oil.
instructions.4: Add the tomatoes and spices and stir until soft, then return the sausage and toss with the pomegranate molasses for 2 minutes.
instructions.5: Serve hot in bread or with fried eggs.

add-253.title: Spicy Egyptian Feshah (Sautéed Lungs)
add-253.culturalNotes: Feshah is a popular Eid al-Adha dish in Egypt; boiling it well first with vinegar and spices removes its smell and tenderises it.

add-253-i2.name: For boiling: onion, bay leaves, cardamom and vinegar

add-253-i7.name: Cumin, chilli, mixed spice and black pepper

instructions.1: Wash the lungs well with water and vinegar and cut into large pieces.
instructions.2: Boil with the onion, bay leaves and cardamom for 45 minutes until cooked, skimming, then drain and cut into small cubes.
instructions.3: Brown the onion in the ghee, then the garlic and peppers.
instructions.4: Add the lungs and stir on high heat until the edges brown, then the tomatoes, paste and spices, stirring until cooked down and dry.
instructions.5: Squeeze over lemon and serve hot with baladi bread.

add-254.title: Egyptian Tripe (Kersha) with Chickpeas
add-254.culturalNotes: Tripe needs careful cleaning and long cooking; a pressure cooker saves a lot of time. The garlic and vinegar dressing is the soul of this Egyptian dish.

add-254-i2.name: For cleaning: coarse salt, vinegar, lemon and flour

add-254-i3.name: For boiling: onion, bay leaves, cardamom and mastic

instructions.1: Scrub the tripe with coarse salt, flour, vinegar and lemon, scrape and rinse several times until white and odour-free.
instructions.2: Blanch 10 minutes and discard the water, then boil in fresh water with the aromatics for 2-3 hours (or an hour in a pressure cooker) until completely tender.
instructions.3: Cut the tripe into small squares, keeping a cup of the broth.
instructions.4: Soften the onion in the ghee, then the garlic, deglaze with the vinegar, then add the tomato juice, spices and broth.
instructions.5: Add the tripe and chickpeas and simmer 20 minutes until thickened.
instructions.6: Serve hot in deep bowls with lemon and bread.

add-255.title: White Bean Salad
add-255.culturalNotes: A salad rich in protein and fibre that makes a light full meal. It improves after an hour in the fridge.

instructions.1: Soak the beans overnight, then boil in fresh water until tender but not mushy; drain and let cool.
instructions.2: Mix the beans with the cucumber, tomato, onion and parsley.
instructions.3: Whisk the lemon, oil, garlic and spices.
instructions.4: Pour the dressing over, toss and leave 15 minutes to absorb the flavours before serving.
